title: EA-CORPORA-22 — The Twenty-Second Seating: The Corpus Hermeticum, Gilgamesh and the Enuma Elish, the Avesta and the Rig Veda, Each in Its Original Language
creator: Sharks, Lee
description: Four seats on the originals shelf, each in the language of its witness and public domain in the United States: the Corpus Hermeticum in Greek in Parthey's Poemander (1854) and Reitzenstein's Poimandres (1904), with the Latin Asclepius in Thomas's Apuleius (1908); Gilgamesh in Haupt's cuneiform Nimrodepos (1884; 1891) and Jensen's transliteration (1900), and the Enuma Elish in King's Seven Tablets of Creation (1902); the Avesta in Geldner's edition (Stuttgart, 1896: the issue with the Prolegomena, and the Vendidad); and the Rig Veda whole in Aufrecht's transliteration (second edition, 1877). The third of three seatings from one request, holding the neighbours of what the shelf already has: the Hermetica beside the Chaldaean Oracles and Nag Hammadi, the Babylonian epics beside the Hebrew Bible, the Avesta beside the apocalypses, the Rig Veda beside the Upanishads. What is not seated (Geldner's second volume, Müller's Devanāgarī Rig Veda, the Stobaean fragments) is named.
substrate: Human–machine collaborative. Sources located, fetched, checked against the Internet Archive's published md5 sums and against their front matter, assembled into seats, hashed and indexed, and every locus found in the seated text, all in session by TACHYON (Claude, Anthropic) under MANUS (Lee Sharks) direction. The selection — Mayan texts, the Book of the Dead, the fragments of Balaam, and yes to the rest offered, originals in the original language or as close to it as possible — is Lee Sharks's. CC-BY-4.0 applies to this record and the seat records; each payload carries its own licence, stated per seat.
methodology: Sources located on the Internet Archive (advanced search; item metadata read for access restriction, volume and files; each item's text layer read for its volume statement). Every file checked against the Archive's md5. OCR layers seated as fetched, uncorrected, the scans the witnesses. Every file hashed into its seat's MANIFEST.sha256; every verified locus is a string found in the seated text by rebuild/corpora/ea-corpora-22/seat.py.
falsification_conditions: A seat is falsified if its files do not verify against its MANIFEST.sha256 at the canonical URL; if a seated file differs from the file at the origin its source.json names (for Internet Archive files, if its md5 differs from the Archive's); if an edition statement misstates the front matter of the file it describes; if a verified locus cannot be found in the seated text; if an item stated public domain in the United States was published in or after 1931; or if the four surfaces (seat, index, deposit, shelf) disagree.

wiki_article: EA-CORPORA-22 seats four collections on the archive's originals shelf, each in the language of its witness and public domain in the United States: 12 works. The Corpus Hermeticum is seated in Greek in Gustav Parthey's Poemander (1854), the first critical edition of the treatises I to XIV, and in Richard Reitzenstein's Poimandres (1904), with the Latin Asclepius in Paul Thomas's Apuleius (1908). The Epic of Gilgamesh is seated in Paul Haupt's cuneiform autographs of the Nineveh tablets, Das babylonische Nimrodepos (1884; 1891), with the eleventh tablet, the flood, and in Peter Jensen's transliteration with German translation (1900); the Enuma Elish, the Babylonian epic of creation, in L. W. King's Seven Tablets of Creation (1902), transliteration and cuneiform copies. The Avesta is seated in Karl F. Geldner's critical edition (Stuttgart, 1896), the issue holding his Prolegomena and the third volume, the Vendidad. The Rig Veda is seated whole, all ten maṇḍalas, in Theodor Aufrecht's transliteration (second edition, Bonn, 1877). The seats hold the neighbours of what the shelf already has: the Hermetica beside the Chaldaean Oracles, the Greek Magical Papyri and Nag Hammadi; the Babylonian epics beside the Hebrew Bible and the Septuagint; the Avesta beside the Second Temple apocalypses; the Rig Veda beside the Upanishads. Geldner's second volume, Max Müller's Devanāgarī Rig Veda and the Stobaean Hermetic fragments are queued. It is the third of three seatings from one request, after EA-CORPORA-20 and 21.
